target: Jujur saja, saya merasa harga sewa di daerah ini semakin tidak masuk akal.
english: Honestly, I feel rent prices in this area are getting more and more unreasonable.
tip: Masuk akal = to make sense (literally 'enters reason'): tidak masuk akal = unreasonable.

target: Kelihatannya kamu kurang tidur, apakah semuanya baik-baik saja?
english: It looks like you haven't had enough sleep — is everything okay?
tip: Kelihatannya = it looks like, built from lihat (see): kelihatannya kamu lelah.

target: Sepertinya saya pernah bertemu dengan dia, tetapi saya lupa di mana.
english: It seems I have met him before, but I forget where.
tip: Sepertinya = it seems, from seperti (like): sepertinya dia sibuk = it seems he's busy.

target: Sepertinya saya salah turun halte, ini bukan daerah yang saya cari.
english: It seems I got off at the wrong stop; this is not the area I am looking for.
tip: Sepertinya = it seems. In Jakarta speech you'll hear kayaknya for this everywhere — recognize it, model sepertinya.

target: Sepertinya enak kalau kita makan bakso hangat saat hujan begini.
english: Seems like it would be nice to have warm meatball soup in rain like this.
tip: Sepertinya enak = 'that sounds nice' — a common way to float a food idea.

target: Saya senang bekerja di sini karena rekan-rekan saling membantu.
english: I enjoy working here because my colleagues help each other.
tip: Saling makes almost any verb mutual: saling membantu = help each other, saling kenal = know each other, saling percaya = trust each other.

target: Saya ikut sedih mendengar kabar tentang kakek kamu.
english: I am also saddened to hear the news about your grandfather.
tip: Ikut + feeling = to share it: saya ikut sedih = I'm sad for you too.

target: Kami sedikit kecewa karena pemandangan dari kamar hotel tidak seindah foto di situs pemesanan.
english: We were a little disappointed because the view from the hotel room was not as beautiful as the photos on the booking site.
tip: Se- + quality = as ... as: seindah foto = as beautiful as the photo.

target: Saya bangga pada tim ini karena kalian tidak pernah menyerah.
english: I am proud of this team because you all never gave up.
tip: Bangga pada + person = proud of: bangga pada tim ini = proud of this team.

target: Ibu khawatir karena kakak belum pulang, padahal sudah hampir tengah malam.
english: Mom is worried because my older sibling is not home yet, even though it is almost midnight.
tip: Padahal = even though / when in fact: belum pulang, padahal sudah malam.

target: Saya berharap kamu bisa hadir di acara pernikahan kami bulan depan.
english: I hope you can come to our wedding next month.
tip: Berharap needs a subject: saya berharap... Semoga opens a wish on its own: Semoga lancar!

target: Semoga keluarga kalian selalu diberi kesehatan dan rezeki.
english: May your family always be blessed with health and good fortune.
tip: Rezeki = livelihood, blessings — a warm everyday wish word: diberi rezeki.

target: Semoga penerbangan kalian nyaman dan sampai dengan selamat.
english: Hope your flight is comfortable and you all arrive safely.
tip: Sampai dengan selamat = arrive safely — the standard send-off for travelers.

target: Saya lebih suka naik kereta daripada pesawat untuk perjalanan pendek.
english: I prefer taking the train to flying for short trips.
tip: Lebih suka X daripada Y = to prefer X to Y: lebih suka kereta daripada pesawat.

target: Ayah lebih suka kopi hitam tanpa gula, katanya lebih nikmat.
english: Dad prefers black coffee without sugar; he says it tastes better.
tip: Katanya = he/she says, they say: katanya lebih nikmat = he says it tastes better.

target: Tidak apa-apa datang terlambat, yang penting kamu datang dengan selamat.
english: It's fine to arrive late; the main thing is you arrive safely.
tip: Yang penting = the main thing is: yang penting kamu selamat = what matters is you're safe.

target: Bagaimana menurut kamu, apakah warna ini cocok untuk ruang tamu?
english: What do you think — does this color suit the living room?
tip: Bagaimana menurut kamu? = What do you think? — literally 'how according to you?'

target: Bagaimana menurut Anda tentang rencana perubahan jam kerja ini?
english: What is your opinion of this plan to change the working hours?
tip: In formal settings (meetings, clients) use Anda instead of kamu: Bagaimana menurut Anda?

target: Saya kurang setuju kalau semua rapat dipindahkan ke hari Jumat.
english: I don't quite agree with moving all the meetings to Friday.
tip: Kurang setuju softens disagreement — politer than a flat tidak setuju.

target: Sebagian teman setuju, sebagian lagi menolak rencana itu.
english: Some friends agree; some others reject the plan.
tip: Sebagian ... sebagian lagi = some ... others: sebagian setuju, sebagian lagi menolak.

target: Jangan takut menyampaikan pendapat, di sini semua ide dihargai.
english: Don't be afraid to voice your opinion; here every idea is appreciated.
tip: Menyampaikan comes from sampai (arrive, reach): to voice something is to make it reach people. Menyampaikan pendapat = get your opinion across.

target: Suasana hati saya langsung membaik setelah mendengar suara anak-anak.
english: My mood improved instantly after hearing the children's voices.
tip: Suasana hati = mood — literally 'atmosphere of the heart'.

target: Kami kaget mendengar harga tanah di daerah ini naik dua kali lipat.
english: We were shocked to hear that land prices in this area have doubled.
tip: Lipat means fold, so dua kali lipat = 'two times folded', like English twofold. It scales: tiga kali lipat = tripled. Naik dua kali lipat = doubled.

target: Pelan-pelan rasa takutnya hilang setelah dia mencoba berenang lagi.
english: Little by little his fear disappeared after he tried swimming again.
tip: Doubling an adjective softens it into a gradual manner: pelan = slow, pelan-pelan = little by little. Pelan-pelan rasa takutnya hilang = the fear slowly faded.

target: Apa pun pendapat orang, keluarga kami tetap bangga pada pilihan kamu.
english: Whatever people's opinions, our family remains proud of your choice.
tip: Apa pun = whatever / no matter what: apa pun pendapat orang = whatever people think.

target: Semakin lama saya tinggal di sini, semakin saya suka kota ini.
english: The longer I live here, the more I like this city.
tip: Semakin ... semakin = the more ... the more: semakin lama, semakin suka = the longer, the more (I) like it.

target: Harga rumah di daerah ini semakin tinggi setiap tahun.
english: House prices in this area get higher and higher every year.
tip: Semakin + adjective alone = getting more and more X: semakin tinggi = higher and higher.

target: Semakin dekat hari keberangkatan, semakin gugup saya.
english: The closer the departure day gets, the more nervous I am.
tip: Ke-...-an makes a noun: berangkat = to depart, keberangkatan = departure.

target: Makin siang, jalanan di kota ini makin panas.
english: The later in the day it gets, the hotter the streets in this city are.
tip: Makin is the everyday spoken short form of semakin: makin siang = the later in the day.

target: Tas ini sama mahalnya dengan tas yang kamu beli kemarin.
english: This bag is as expensive as the bag you bought yesterday.
tip: Sama + adjective + -nya + dengan = as ... as: sama mahalnya dengan = as expensive as.
